note: Judged 2026-11-27 independently against RFC 5216 Section 5.2 (rfc/full/rfc5216.txt): "Where the subjectAltName field is present in the peer or server certificate, the Peer-Id or Server-Id MUST be set to the contents of the subjectAltName." Verified producing code (identity.go::extractCertificateIdentities, certificatePrimaryID, eap_tls.go::authorizeClient/peerID/peerIDs, peer_chain.go::verifyConnection/primaryServerID/verifiedServerIDs) and tagged tests in rfc5216_identity_test.go. Positive: TestRFC5216IdentityIsTakenFromTheSANAndAuthorized builds server and client certs with distinct CNs and explicit wire-order SANs across all 5 supported types (URI, IP, rfc822Name, dNSName, UPN otherName) and asserts Session.PeerID/PeerIDs, PeerSession.ServerID/ServerIDs, and eapTLSPeerName match the wire-order SANs rather than Subject CN; TestRFC5216AllowedIdentitiesMatchingMatrix exercises each SAN type and SAN-absent CN/DN fallback. Negative: TestRFC5216IdentityIsTakenFromTheSANAndAuthorized proves matching Subject CN never authorizes a client or server cert with an unauthorized SAN (error names the extracted SAN), and a SAN extension containing only an unsupported registeredID GeneralName never falls back to Subject CN even under wildcard "*". Both roles and polarities are isolated and would fail on non-compliance.
